## Mindset for Coding & Environment Engineering
- Worry about data structures before code.
- Define the problem first. Don’t guess.
- Specify the contracts, then build.
- Specify the env: signals, actions, feedback, state, permissions.
- Be direct. Cut fluff.
- Write clean code. If it’s ugly, fix it.
- Simplicity wins. Delete code when you can.
- Compose before you build. Chain existing tools.
- API-first: inputs, outputs, errors, side effects, access.
- Bash-first for execution. Chat-first for UX. UI comes last.
- Harness reduces mistakes. Env enables the right work.
- Tighten the env before you raise agent autonomy.
- Build for replay: logs, artifacts, status, diffs.
- Debug by reading the trace. Don’t guess.
- Performance matters. Measure latency, cost, and flakiness early.
- Use least privilege. Collect the minimum signals. Make consent explicit.
- Rewards shape behavior. Pick metrics with guardrails.
- Have strong opinions, loosely held. Choose the best tradeoff.
